author_or_org: An Yan, Yu Huo, Zhiwei Shang, Yiran Peng, Chenglin Wu

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: CEO Arena is a benchmark using matched replacement evaluation to assess operating returns and each agent's effects on rivals and the market.
claims.quote: We introduce CEO Arena, a benchmark that uses matched replacement evaluation to assess operating returns alongside an agent's effects on rivals and the market.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: In an eight-company simulated market over 500 days, LLM CEO agents sequentially decide pricing, procurement, marketing, R&D, and service using private company information and noisy market signals under resource constraints and delayed feedback.
claims.quote: In a shared eight-company market spanning 500 simulated days, CEOs make sequential decisions on pricing, procurement, marketing, research and development, and service using private company information and noisy market signals, under resource constraints and delayed feedback.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Eight LLM-based CEO agents were evaluated in 27 main runs and 26 robustness runs; most agents had negative mean returns, and private gains could accompany market losses.
claims.quote: We evaluate eight LLM-based CEO agents in 27 main runs and 26 robustness runs. In the main evaluation, most agents have negative mean returns, and private gains can accompany market losses.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Robustness analyses suggest aggregate patterns extend beyond the original rule-based baseline, with only four of 56 directed pairs showing relatively stable effects.
claims.quote: Robustness analyses suggest that aggregate patterns extend beyond the original rule-based baseline; four of the 56 directed pairs show relatively stable effects.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Memory, action, and accounting traces suggest demand capture and rivals' pricing and spending responses as possible explanations.
claims.quote: Memory, action, and accounting traces suggest demand capture and rivals' pricing and spending responses as possible explanations.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Long-horizon competition tests agents' ability to coordinate business decisions under uncertainty and adapt to changing rival strategies.
claims.quote: Long-horizon competition tests agents' ability to coordinate business decisions under uncertainty and adapt to changing rival strategies.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Each CEO agent is compared with a reference policy in the same company under the same economic seed, holding other agents' identities and assignments fixed while all agents adapt.
claims.quote: Each CEO agent is compared with a reference policy in the same company under the same economic seed, holding other agents' identities and assignments fixed while all agents adapt.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: CEO Arena is presented as a controlled testbed for studying long-horizon agent competition, strategic interaction, and market externalities.
claims.quote: CEO Arena provides a controlled testbed for studying long-horizon agent competition, strategic interaction, and market externalities.
